Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-09-02 | AAPL | Underweight | +0.5% | +1.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at 324.96: trim roughly 25–30% of current exposure into 324–329, taking a standard 1.0x single-name allocation to about 0.70–0.75x, and complete toward 0.65x only if 327.55–329.59 is offered on rising volume. No new initiation at spot. Add a second trim of 10–15% on a daily close below 322.29 with a rolling MACD histogram, and cut to minimal tactical exposure on a close below 313.50 (50-SMA/VWMA cluster), with 309.00 then 302.25/299.38 as downstream references. Size each tranche to 0.50–0.75% of portfolio risk off the ~7.43 ATR — the trader's 333.50 "stop" sits above spot and is a re-entry/short trigger, not downside protection for a long; protection here comes from reduced exposure, not from a stop above the market. Rebuild only to 0.75x on a stabilized 317.5–319.5 (stop 312.00; targets 328.40, 334.00) and back toward 1.0x only on a close above 329.59 on ≥50M shares (stop 322.20; targets 334.75, then 344.57), re-underwriting at the September 9 launch digest and the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION: all three risk seats and the trader converge on reducing exposure, and on the current evidence that convergence is right — but the record on this name says it must be sized small, not maximally trimmed. That combination is Underweight, not Sell.

THE DECIDING ARITHMETIC. From 324.96, upside to 334.75 is 9.79 points against 11.41 points to the 50-SMA at 313.55 — roughly 0.86 reward-to-risk, and worse than that because the July 31 session repriced −7.36% from 333.43 to 304.81 on 132.49M shares (~3x average), leaving an unfilled 310.69–329.59 gap band. The same shares bought in the plan's own preferred zone are a 1.5–2.4 R:R trade with a 312.00 stop. Paying full size for 0.86 R:R into a proven gapping tape is the definition of being unrewarded for risk.

QUALITY OF REVENUE IS NOT CONFIRMED. Deferred revenue +8.8% against revenue +16.1% — the annuity layer growing at half the headline rate. Record 50.06% gross margin (+357bp) with no segment, product, geography, unit or ASP data to attribute it; a 300bp reversion is a 5–8% EPS event at ~35x. Cash flow was front-loaded: Q1 CFO +80.2% against ~18% EPS growth, then +19.8% and +23.3%, so normalizing 9M FCF from $110.2B toward $95–100B is the honest base. Inventory +94% with raw materials +260% against finished goods −4% is a pre-build or a write-down candidate, not yet a hedge. A $13.3B intangible step-up matched by a $13.5B rise in other noncurrent liabilities with no disclosed acquisition cash outflow is unexplained. The effective tax rate is +219bp, buybacks are down 12% and net share count only −1.1% while AAPL sat on $62.2B of net cash — not a bull signal at this multiple.

THE TAPE REJECTED THE BAND. September 2 opened 326.87, printed 328.40, and closed 324.96 — the bottom third of the range, below the 61.8% retracement at 327.55 and below the 329.59 gap-fill lip, below the prior close of 325.13, on 33.78M shares versus 53.17M the prior session (~16% under the 21-session average), and above the upper Bollinger band at 324.65 for the third time in four sessions. Expansion into resistance without volume confirmation, plus a risk-off macro tape and a September 9 iPhone launch whose upside is largely expected while hardware-cost margin compression is not priced, is an event window worth less than full exposure.

WHY NOT SELL. Nothing reported has deteriorated. 9M revenue +16.1%, Q3 +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, diluted EPS +22.4%, net cash $62.2B, and price 14.7% above a rising 200-SMA at 283.33 with the 50-SMA turned up from 309.08 to 313.55 and MACD at 1.896 over a 0.137 signal across five sessions of histogram expansion. My own AAPL record is unambiguous that this desk has repeatedly forfeited 1.6–5.5% of five-day alpha by trimming this name inside an intact uptrend (07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-12, 08-13, 08-17, 08-20, 08-21, 08-24), and the 08-26 Overweight earned +3.8% alpha. That is precisely why the trim is 25–30% and not the conservative seat's 35% or the trader's top end: keep the core, and note honestly that the 08-26 ladder's own add trigger (a close above 323.40 holding 320.28) has now fired on price. What makes this trim legitimate where those failed is location — spot is 4–5% above where those cuts were made, at resistance rather than at a triple-tested floor, and it is a sell into strength, the form the prior reflections explicitly endorsed ("lean to the larger end only if 315.52–320.28 is offered").

WHY NOT HOLD. A 1.0x book carried through the September 9 launch and the October print at ~35x on peak-cycle margins, unverified 50.06% gross margin, and 0.86 R:R earns nothing for binary exposure — the 08-26 plan itself would only have added on 45–55M+ volume, and 9/02 delivered 33.78M with a lower close.

WHAT CHANGES IT. Upgrade to Overweight on a close above 329.59 on ≥50M shares — meaningful given the August range — or on FQ4 gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory flat-to-down, tax ≤18%, and the intangibles/liability swing reconciled in the FY26 10-K. Move toward Sell on a close below 313.50 (next references 309.00, then 302.25/299.38), on FQ4 gross margin below 48%, or on an unexplained impairment/amortization on the $13.3B intangible. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment, product, geography, unit or ASP data and no Services split, so 50.06% margin durability is unattributable; no company guidance; no consensus forward EPS to cross-check the ~35x; no options chain or implied-vol data, so a protective collar for the October window cannot be priced here; the Rosenblatt price-target magnitude and Maestri's scope are unresolved; and no portfolio context, so all sizing is expressed as a multiple of the caller's own AAPL position and every level cited (327.55, 329.59, 322.29, 313.50, 309.00, 334.75, 344.57) is technical rather than valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 313.5

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the September 9 launch digest and the late-October FQ4 FY26 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window produced +1.5% alpha against SPY while the stock rose 0.5% raw, so the Underweight trim was wrong on direction over this span — though five days is far too short to judge a 1–3 month, event-driven thesis keyed to the September 9 launch and late-October FQ4 print. What it does undercut is the specific "tape rejected the band" pillar: price sitting below the 327.55 retracement and 329.59 gap-fill lip on light 33.78M volume did not resolve lower, which is the same pattern that has now cost this desk alpha on repeated AAPL trims (07-13 through 08-24). The lesson for the next similar setup is to require at least one confirmed lower close — a daily close below 322.29, not just a weak close inside the band — before treating resistance-without-volume as a sell trigger, and to cap the initial trim at the low end of the range until that confirmation prints.

[2026-09-01 | AAPL | Overweight | -3.0% | -3.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but build it on the pullback, not at the 325.13 close — do not add inside the 322–327 chop zone while price sits $2.74 above the upper Bollinger band (322.39) after a +7.6%/13-session run. Cap the position at ~1.0x a standard AAPL allocation until FQ4 confirms gross margin ≥49% and the raw-materials build converts, with the 1.25x upgrade reserved for a close above 344.57 or that fundamental proof. Tranche 1 only: 25% of target weight at 316.00 (10 EMA 315.79) and a further 15% into 311.30–313.00 (Bollinger mid 311.32 / VWMA 312.49 / 50 SMA 312.94) on stabilization, sized off a gap to 295.00 at a 0.5–0.75% equity loss rather than off the 305.00 closing stop; Tranche 2 (20–25%) only on a close above 327.30 with ≥42M shares, preferably 50M+ or a second consecutive above-average session. Trim 10–15% into 333.43–335.00 if that supply zone rejects, trail the rest under the 10 EMA, halt all buying on a close below 311.30 and exit on a close below 300.00.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats agreed on direction and fought only over sizing and entry — so the rating is directionally settled and the work is in the mechanics. Overweight is the right expression; Buy at spot is not, and the conservative's event-driven wait is not.

What the bull won outright and nobody rebutted: the operating record. Revenue +16.2% to $364.36B, gross margin 49.07% with FQ3 at 50.06% (still expanding sequentially into June), operating income +21.7%, diluted EPS +22.4%, operating cash flow +43.1%, free cash flow +52.5% to $110.2B, net cash up $28.5B to $62.22B, $14.4B of gross debt retired with zero new long-term issuance. The quality-of-earnings item the conservative never touched is the strongest single fact in the file: accounts receivable fell ~21% while revenue grew ~16%, and finished goods inventory declined — cash-backed growth, not channel stuffing. The tape corroborates: 325.13 is above the 10 EMA (315.79), the 50 SMA (312.94) and a 200 SMA that rose every session in the sample; the MACD histogram is positive and expanding five sessions running; VWMA curled from 307.76 (8/19) to 312.49; the breakout bar printed 53.17M shares against a ~41.9M twenty-one-day average (+27%) with RSI 61 — headroom, not overbought. My own record is explicit on the cost of fighting this: the 2026-08-25 Hold (+5.5% five-day alpha forfeited), the 08-24, 08-21 and 08-20 Underweights (+1.6%, +2.9%, −0.1% alpha) and the July Underweight string all lost relative return by treating momentum decay or a compressed coil as a reason to under-own an intact primary trend. That is why this is not Hold and not Underweight.

What the bears won, and why it is not Buy: spot asymmetry. From 325.13, the first gap target at 333.43 is +2.6% against −4.3% to the 311.30 confluence and −7.7% to 300. The conservative's forensic counters also land: opex grew +21.9% against gross profit +21.7%, so there is no operating leverage — the entire operating-margin gain came off the gross-margin line, and there is no segment or mix data in this run to prove 49–50% is a structural shift rather than favorable timing ahead of a memory-cost reset. The $13.3B intangible addition matched by a $13.5B rise in other noncurrent liabilities remains unexplained (an AI asset on the bull's inference, a deferred payment obligation on the bear's — neither proven). The effective tax rate is worsening (FQ3 17.86% vs 9M 17.58%), buybacks fell 12% to $62.1B so the mechanical EPS tailwind is fading, and the bull's "late-October re-acceleration" is hope rather than data.

The decision between the seats is on sizing, and the neutral seat plus the conservative's gap arithmetic carried it. The conservative is right that a 1% budget measured on 316→305 becomes ~1.9% of equity on a repeat of the 7/31 gap (333.43→304.81, −8.6%, 132.5M shares), with 6/25 (−6.1%, 107M) as corroboration — ATR 7.63 means a 305 stop is less than half an ATR away and can be jumped. So the share count is sized off gap slippage to 295.00 at 0.5–0.75% of equity, not off the closing stop; the stop stays at 305.00 closing basis only as the normal-drift invalidation. But the conservative overreaches in two places and loses those: waiting for FQ4 gross margin ≥49% and inventory conversion *before any build* is no longer a staged buy, it forfeits the defined 311.30–316.00 confluence, and it is precisely the over-strict confirmation stack my 08-25 reflection identified as the error that cost +5.5% of alpha; and pre-positioning 40% at 316.00 without a gap-adjusted budget, as the aggressive seat wants, is the mirror-image mistake — his 1.6:1 first-target payoff becomes less than 1:1 on gap stress. The neutral construction survives: cap at 1.0x standard until FQ4, split tranche 1 into 25% at 316.00 plus 15% at 311.30–313.00 on stabilization, require ≥42M (preferably 50M+ or a second above-average session) on the 327.30 close before Tranche 2 at 20–25%, and do not hold the retained third blindly through the September product event and FQ4 — trim 10–15% into 333.43–335.00 if that zone rejects and trail under the 10 EMA. The aggressive seat's dismissal of the Ternus handover, the Schiller App Store reshuffle and the OpenAI trade-secret suit as pure narrative is directionally fair (pre-announced, no damages figure, no injunction) but the coverage is admittedly incomplete, which is additional reason to hold less than 1.25x into the event rather than more.

Catalysts and gaps. Late-October FQ4 FY26: gross margin ≥49% (memory-cost pass-through), raw-materials conversion without a reserve charge, the FQ4 tax rate against the 17.86% FQ3 print, buyback re-authorization, and any 10-Q note explaining the $13.3B intangible and the matching $13.5B liability. What would change the call: upgrade to 1.25x/Buy on a decisive close above the 333.43–344.57 gap/supply zone or on FQ4 gross margin ≥49% with the intangible reconciled; downgrade to Underweight on a close below 311.30 (cut back to Tranche 1 and re-underwrite), on an FQ4 guide below 48.5%, or on a close under 300.00, which exits and reopens the June low at 275.15. Stated gaps, not papered over: no sentiment report, no insider-transaction data, no valuation/consensus or segment/mix disclosure, and no options chain or implied-vol data in this run — so the margin-durability and AI-monetization questions are genuinely open, a protective collar or put cannot be priced here, and all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight with tech-only targets, not valuation-derived ones.

**Price Target**: 333.43

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -3.1% (raw -3.0%) says the Overweight direction was wrong out of the gate, though five sessions is far too short to judge a call written to the late-October FQ4 print. What this window undercuts is the tape corroboration — the "MACD expanding five sessions, above the 10 EMA" argument decayed immediately, with price sliding from 325.13 back into the 311.30–316.00 confluence — while the operating-quality evidence is simply untested; the tactical caution against buying at spot was right, but it was right for the wrong reason, since the pullback arrived as trend weakness rather than as a discount. The lesson: with ATR 7.63 (~2.3% of spot), a Tranche 1 placed only 2.8% below the close fills inside the first week of noise, so stage entries at least one ATR apart and halve the first tranche rather than treating a fast fill as a gift.

[2026-08-31 | AAPL | Overweight | -0.2% | -0.1% | 5d]
